title: Urban Green Spaces and Psychosocial Well-Being: Findings from Structural Equation Modeling in Baku
content: Urban green spaces (UGS) are increasingly recognized as important environmental resources that contribute to public health and psychological well-being in rapidly urbanizing cities. This study examines the relationship between urban green space usage and mental health outcomes, specifically psychological well-being (WHO-5) and anxiety (GAD-7), among residents of Baku, Azerbaijan. The study also aims to identify key patterns of green space use and evaluate their potential effects using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). A cross-sectional design was employed, and data were collected using validated instruments, including the WHO-5 Well-Being Index and the GAD-7 Anxiety Scale, alongside a structured questionnaire assessing green space usage behaviors. The sample primarily consisted of students and young adults. Descriptive analyses were used to examine demographic characteristics and usage patterns, while SEM was applied to test the relationships between variables. The findings revealed that frequency of park visits, proximity to green spaces, and duration of park use did not have statistically significant direct effects on either psychological well-being or anxiety. However, a significant negative relationship was observed between well-being and anxiety, indicating that higher levels of well-being are associated with lower anxiety symptoms. The results suggest that green space usage alone may not directly predict mental health outcomes in the context of Baku, where green space availability and usage patterns are relatively limited and primarily short-term. Overall, the study highlights the importance of considering qualitative and contextual factors in understanding the mental health benefits of urban green spaces. The findings provide valuable implications for urban planning and public health policies aimed at improving the design, accessibility, and functionality of green spaces to better support psychological well-being in urban populations.
